summary.oneLiner: HFL delivered record FY26 profitability driven by capex completion across 5 verticals, with FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220cr anchored on full utilization of newly commissioned assets and GST reclassification shifting revenue recognition without impacting EBITDA or PAT.

one-line thesis: HFL delivered record FY26 profitability driven by capex completion across 5 verticals, with FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220cr anchored on full utilization of newly commissioned assets and GST reclassification shifting revenue recognition without impacting EBITDA or PAT.
financial scorecard: revenue: +17% YoY to INR4,264cr (FY26); EBITDA/margin: +20% YoY to INR377cr (FY26), margin expanded; PAT (rptd): +29% YoY to INR149cr (FY26); PAT (normalized): adjusted for underutilized assets, ROCE at 18.9%; order book: INR150cr new contracts signed for FY27; net debt: net debt-to-equity at 0.84x (within 1x target), cash flow impacted by GST inverted duty structure and inventory buildup
guidance: revenue growth: not quantified but volumes expected to jump >50% in ice cream alone; margin: PAT guidance INR200-220cr (40-50% YoY growth); order inflow: INR150cr new projects signed (beverages INR50cr, HPC INR50cr, ice cream INR50cr); capex/commissioning: FY27 capex to be funded from internal accruals, Panipat (Apr'26), Aurangabad bottle, Silvassa detergent, Lucknow bar, Baddi Ayurveda facility to commission in FY27
order book & pipeline: INR150 crores in new contracts signed since April 2026: INR50cr beverages, INR50cr HPC, INR50cr ice cream (brownfield expansion in Lucknow & Panipat)
segment / subsidiary detail: Food & Beverages: scaling dairy, snacks, entering Greek yogurt; Beverages: new bottle capacity in Aurangabad & South India; Ice Cream: backward integration via cone & stick manufacturing; HPC: Aurangabad Personal Care integrated, Silvassa liquid detergent & Lucknow bar facility under construction; Healthcare: Ayurvedic facility at Baddi under development; Footwear: raw material cost pressure (petrochemicals +50-60%), capacity expansion in North/South India
growth verticals / optionality: Beverage bottling to become India's largest independent bottler; Ayurveda wellness manufacturing as new vertical; D2C & premium product focus in HPC; ice cream volume growth via backward integration; footwear expansion into athleisure & comfort segments
margins & cost dynamics: Footwear EBITDA pressured by 50-60% petrochemical price rise; other segments passed on raw material costs; GST inverted duty structure (5% on food vs higher on packaging) causing working capital strain and revenue recognition shift; no margin erosion expected post-reclassification
capex / expansion: FY26 capex: INR700cr+; FY27 capex: INR150cr new contracts signed (not guidance); gross block to reach INR2,150cr by FY27 end; funding from internal accruals; Panipat (INR200cr), Aurangabad, Silvassa, Lucknow, Baddi facilities commissioned or under construction
capital allocation: 60% dedicated / 40% shared manufacturing capex split maintained; ROCE threshold of 18% for all projects; PAT guidance INR200-220cr prioritized over revenue growth; no external funding planned; reinvestment in high-ROCE shared manufacturing and backward integration
risks & watch-items: Footwear raw material volatility (petrochemicals); GST reclassification delays with customers; geopolitical supply chain disruptions; underutilized assets impacting near-term ROCE until FY27 ramp-up; customer confidentiality limiting segment disclosure
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; emphasized operational execution, capex discipline, and PAT guidance; transparent on accounting adjustments; agnostic on segments but focused on 20% EBITDA growth and 18% ROCE across divisions
non-obvious takeaways: GST inverted duty structure reclassification will reduce reported revenue but improve EBITDA/PAT margins (denominator effect); Panipat ice cream plant alone adds 50% to FY26 ice cream volume; Baddi acquisition accounting difference of INR220cr explains capital employed reconciliation gap; footwear is 100% shared manufacturing (higher ROCE target) despite current cost pressure

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as the "Most Diversified Contract Manufacturer in India", spanning five business segments — Home & Personal Care, Food & Beverages, Ice Cream, Healthcare and Footwear — with 35+ years of manufacturing experience and 42 factories across 12 states.
- Segment leadership claims made in the deck: "India's largest independent bottler" (listed against Food & Beverages), "India's largest vertically integrated contract manufacturer" (listed against Ice Cream), "India's leading home & personal care contract manufacturers", "India's trusted healthcare & wellness manufacturing partner" and an "Emerging footwear contract manufacturing platform".
- Moat is framed as trust and brand custodianship: long-standing partnerships with leading global and Indian consumer brands built on "trust, confidentiality, and consistent delivery", safeguarding customer IP and protecting brand integrity.
- Dedicated facilities create "customized infrastructure" and "high switching costs and strong customer retention", with an average contract tenure of 8+ years on a Rs. 1,123 crore dedicated manufacturing gross block.
- Positioned as a one-stop partner offering integrated services from product innovation and quality testing through to large-scale manufacturing, with the ability to create tailored formulations across the spectrum.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Footwear headwinds] Results were impacted by Middle East crisis-led raw material inflation and temporary supply-chain disruption in the Footwear Division affecting material availability, cost and production, plus New Labour Code wage increases effective April 1; customer pass-through discussions are underway.
- [Regulatory / export] Initiated the Class 3 Medical Device certification process at the Chennai facility for medicated plasters, supporting expansion into the EU and UK markets.
- [Acquisition] The Aurangabad personal care acquisition has been fully integrated, production stabilized and all systems and processes are fully operational.
- [Guidance] FY27 PAT guidance of Rs. 200-220 Cr reaffirmed, which the deck describes as 34-48% growth over FY26.
- [Market context] Deck cites third-party market sizes for its end-markets, including India's personal care market at Rs. 2,25,000 Cr in 2025 growing at ~14-15% CAGR to 2030, home care at Rs. 72,000 Cr in 2025 at ~11% CAGR, packaged food at US$129.18 Bn in 2025 at ~6.2% CAGR to 2034, beverages at US$80.11 Bn in 2025 at ~6.8% CAGR to 2035, ice cream at US$2.07 Bn in 2024 at ~13% CAGR to 2030, OTC healthcare & wellness at Rs. 47,000 Cr in 2024 at ~13% CAGR and footwear at US$18.8 Bn in 2024 at ~12.4% CAGR.
